Let’s dive into Chapter 7: Delivering a Remarkable Customer Experience.
So, a lead finally becomes a customer. But you know what? That’s just the beginning. What happens after the sale—that’s what really counts. It’s these moments that decide if someone comes back, tells their friends, or simply fades away.
Think about the last time you checked into a hotel. Maybe you found a handwritten note waiting for you, with your name on it, and your favorite snack right there on the table. Feels special, doesn’t it? Little gestures like that can turn something ordinary into something unforgettable. And honestly, it doesn’t matter if you run a huge company or a small shop—this approach works anywhere.
So, what does delivering a truly remarkable experience look like?
First, there’s onboarding. Guide your new customers step by step, so they feel supported and confident right from the start.
Then, keep the conversation going. Let folks know what’s coming up, what to expect, and exactly how they can reach out if they need help. Consistent communication makes people feel cared for.
And don’t forget to surprise and delight. Maybe it’s a bonus resource, a thank-you note, or a quick check-in call. Those unexpected touches can make someone’s day.
Picture this: a local gym welcomes a new member with a custom workout plan, then checks in after their first week. It’s not just about making a sale—it’s about supporting someone’s journey.
Also, don’t be afraid to ask for feedback. When you genuinely listen and make changes based on what customers share, it shows you’re committed to getting better and better.
Here are a few key practices to keep in mind:
Set clear expectations. Let people know what’s happening and when.
If a problem comes up, jump on it quickly—with empathy and a sense of urgency.
And when your customers hit a milestone, or celebrate an anniversary—recognize it! Celebrate right along with them.
When you focus on what happens after the sale, you’re not just building transactions—you’re building loyalty. Happy customers come back more often, spend more, and can’t wait to tell others about you.
This is where real advocacy starts—one thoughtful interaction at a time.
